subject: [PATCH] btrfs: keep a logged extent allocated when its ordered extent fails

reviews.author: Filipe Manana
reviews.summary: Filipe Manana noted that there are valid points from Sashiko regarding writes into prealloc extents, which he considers relevant to the current patch and suggests reviewing them.
reviews.raw_body:
Since we are here, we can fix the original comment and add punctuation.

Looks good in general, but there are some valid points from Sashiko
regarding writes into prealloc extents:

https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/54da67463c57f41302f8456a8a7a1190dcb65ae2.1794266796.git.loemra.dev%40gmail.com

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch prevents a logged extent in Btrfs from being freed when its ordered extent fails, which can lead to data corruption and checksum errors during log replay after a transaction abort. The fix involves not freeing the extent of a failed ordered extent that was logged by a fast fsync, but instead keeping it out of the free space cache until the next mount. This ensures that the log replay points to the correct blocks with the correct checksums. The patch also includes additional checks and error handling to prevent similar issues from occurring in other scenarios.
